Hi Sophia — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on the residency constraints you mentioned on the call (EU-only for customer data, APAC latency-sensitive reads for a subset of traffic).

Summary of needs we heard:
- Primary requirement: customer PII and transaction logs must remain in EU jurisdiction (cannot leave EU).
- Secondary need: low-latency inference for APAC users for product recommendation flows (read-only inference ok, no long-term storage requirement).
- Procurement: you'd like procurement and architecture artifacts to share with security and legal.

Recommended pilot (low-friction, measurable):
1) Dedicated capacity in EU (reserved GPU pool) for all write/PII-bearing traffic — satisfies data residency and auditability.
2) Hosted API endpoints in APAC (standard Redwood API) for read-latency traffic with strict routing rules and no long-term persistence of request payloads.
3) Smart routing with prefix-based keys: EU requests -> EU Dedicated; APAC requests -> APAC Hosted; fallback to EU Dedicated if APAC region unavailable (configurable).

Why this path? It gives you EU data residency guarantees and auditability (Dedicated = isolated capacity + audit logs) while keeping launch velocity and cost control in APAC via Hosted. If you need a fully private VPC later in APAC, we can convert the Hosted APAC footprint to Private without changing client-side integration.

Attachments: I attached a short options doc and a checklist for security/procurement (redwood-deployment-options.pdf, eu-apac-deployment-checklist.xlsx).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm: (a) EU data residency applies to both request bodies and logs? (b) Any regulatory requirement for cross-border telemetry (metrics/traces)?
- If yes to (a), we’ll prepare a brief SOW and a cost delta for Dedicated EU capacity + Hosted APAC layer.
- Suggest a 60-minute follow-up with your security architect and procurement — proposed slots next Tue/Wed.

Thanks — Evelyn

Hi Sophia — quick technical note to address the security questions and pricing delta so procurement has something concrete. Pasting the short bullets here; a one-page diagram is attached (see redwood-deployment-options.pdf).

Technical points:
- Dedicated (EU): data plane (inference + KV cache) runs in your reserved GPU pool in eu-west-1. Customer-provisioned KMS or Redwood-managed KMS with EU-only key residency supported. Audit logs (request metadata, admin actions) stored in EU S3 bucket; retention configurable and included in Dedicated contract.
- Hosted (APAC): inference endpoints in ap-southeast-1 region. By default Hosted retains short-term telemetry (30 days); for this pilot we’ll set retention to 7 days and disable payload persistence. No PII will be routed to Hosted — tokenized inputs only.
- Routing: we’ll implement region-based routing rules at the API gateway and client-side SDK can include a 'region_hint' header. Fallback logic: APAC -> EU Dedicated if APAC capacity is unavailable for a configured grace period.
- Operational tradeoffs: Dedicated adds fixed monthly commit and predictable latency for writes. Hosted is variable cost-per-token but lower ops lead time. Conversion path: Hosted -> Private VPC is supported and preserves API surface.

Pricing delta (very rough, preliminary):
- EU Dedicated baseline (monthly commit): $12,000/mo (includes 4x reserved GPUs, monitoring, 99.9% uptime SLA).
- Hosted APAC incremental traffic: estimated $0.0009/token for peak recommendation traffic; expect $6k–$9k/mo depending on traffic shape.
- One-time onboarding + architecture pack: $8k (includes diagram, KMS integration plan, and SOC2 evidence bundle).

If that aligns, we’ll convert this into a short statement of work with exact SKU-level pricing. For security: attached checklist includes the KMS options and logging endpoints (eu-apac-deployment-checklist.xlsx).

Next step: Evelyn will coordinate the Thursday call with security + procurement and we’ll bring an infra engineer.
